issues.description: The problem description and template expect measurement probabilities to be computed from the squared magnitude (|amplitude|^2) of complex amplitudes, but the solution implementation in tensor_networks.py computes probabilities as np.real(a**2). Using a**2 and taking the real part is not equivalent to |a|^2 for complex amplitudes and can produce incorrect or negative probabilities, which will break sampling and contradict the specification in the exercise description.
issues.suggestedFix: Compute probabilities from amplitudes using the squared magnitude, e.g. probabilities = [np.abs(a)**2 for a in amplitudes] (or np.real_if_close(np.abs(a)**2) if needed). Ensure the resulting probabilities are non-negative and normalized before sampling.
